Instructions: Read the following code snippets and identify their time complexity using Big O notation.

Snippet 1:

function findMax(arr) {
let max = arr[0];
for (let i = 1; i < arr.length; i++) {
if (arr[i] > max) {
max = arr[i];
}
}
return max;
}

Snippet 2:

function findDuplicates(arr) {
for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
for (let j = i + 1; j < arr.length; j++) {
if (arr[i] === arr[j]) {
return true;
}
}
}
return false;
}

Snippet 3:

function binarySearch(arr, target) {
let left = 0;
let right = arr.length - 1;
while (left <= right) {
let mid = Math.floor((left + right) / 2);
if (arr[mid] === target) return mid;
if (arr[mid] < target) left = mid + 1;
else right = mid - 1;
}
return -1;
}

questions.texte: Analyse each code snippet and determine its time complexity.
questions.reponse: Snippet 1: O(n) - Linear time. Snippet 2: O(n²) - Quadratic time. Snippet 3: O(log n) - Logarithmic time.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the time complexity of Snippet 1? Explain your reasoning.
sousQuestions.reponse: O(n) - Linear time. The function iterates through the array once, performing a constant-time operation for each element.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the time complexity of Snippet 2? Explain your reasoning.
sousQuestions.reponse: O(n²) - Quadratic time. The nested loops cause the function to compare each element with every other element.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the time complexity of Snippet 3? Explain your reasoning.
sousQuestions.reponse: O(log n) - Logarithmic time. Binary search divides the search space in half at each step, reducing the problem size exponentially.

Instructions: You are in a whiteboard coding interview. The interviewer asks you to solve the following problem. Write a script of what you would say to explain your thought process.

Problem: Given an array of integers, find the two numbers that add up to a specific target sum. Return the indices of the two numbers.

Example: Input: nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9 → Output: [0, 1]

questions.texte: Write a script (200-300 words) explaining your thought process to the interviewer. Include: clarifying questions, initial approach, optimization discussion, and final solution.
questions.reponse: Exemple de réponse : 'First, let me clarify the problem. Can I assume the input array is sorted? Can I use the same element twice? Are there always exactly two numbers that add up to the target? ...' 'My initial approach would be a brute force solution with two nested loops, which would have O(n²) time complexity. But I think we can do better. We could use a hash map to store the complement of each number. This would give us O(n) time complexity...'

Instructions: You are in a whiteboard coding interview. Solve the following problem and explain your solution verbally.

Problem: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. You may assume that each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

Example: Input: nums = [3, 2, 4], target = 6 → Output: [1, 2]

Write your solution in JavaScript and explain:

  • Your approach and why you chose it
  • The time and space complexity
  • Any edge cases you considered

questions.texte: Write the JavaScript solution and explain your approach.
questions.reponse: function twoSum(nums, target) { const map = new Map(); for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) { const complement = target - nums[i]; if (map.has(complement)) { return [map.get(complement), i]; } map.set(nums[i], i); } return []; } Time complexity: O(n). Space complexity: O(n).

Instructions: For each of the following solutions, identify the time complexity and space complexity, and justify your answers.

Solution A:

function factorial(n) {
if (n <= 1) return 1;
return n * factorial(n - 1);
}

Solution B:

function fibonacci(n) {
let memo = [0, 1];
for (let i = 2; i <= n; i++) {
memo[i] = memo[i-1] + memo[i-2];
}
return memo[n];
}

questions.texte: Analyse each solution and determine its time and space complexity.
questions.reponse: Solution A: Time = O(n), Space = O(n) due to recursion stack. Solution B: Time = O(n), Space = O(n) for the memo array.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the time complexity of Solution A? Justify your answer.
sousQuestions.reponse: O(n) - The function makes one recursive call per level, going from n down to 1.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the space complexity of Solution A? Justify your answer.
sousQuestions.reponse: O(n) - Each recursive call adds a frame to the call stack until the base case is reached.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the time complexity of Solution B? Justify your answer.
sousQuestions.reponse: O(n) - The loop runs n times, performing constant-time operations.

Instructions: You have written the following solution for the Two Sum problem. The interviewer asks you to test and debug your solution verbally. Write a script of how you would walk through the testing process.

function twoSum(nums, target) {
const map = {};
for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
const complement = target - nums[i];
if (map[complement] !== undefined) {
return [map[complement], i];
}
map[nums[i]] = i;
}
return [];
}

questions.texte: Write a script (200-300 words) explaining how you would test this solution with different test cases, including edge cases.

Now, let me test edge cases: empty array, array with one element, negative numbers, duplicates, and very large numbers... I should also test cases where there is no solution (though the problem says there is always one)...'

Instructions: The following code has a bug. Identify the bug and fix it. Then explain the bug to the interviewer as you would in a whiteboard session.

function findMaxSubarraySum(arr) {
let maxSum = 0;
let currentSum = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
currentSum += arr[i];
if (currentSum > maxSum) {
maxSum = currentSum;
}
if (currentSum < 0) {
currentSum = 0;
}
}
return maxSum;
}

questions.texte: Identify the bug in this code and explain how to fix it.
questions.reponse: The bug is that maxSum is initialized to 0, which fails for arrays with all negative numbers. The fix is to initialize maxSum to -Infinity or arr[0].

sousQuestions.texte: What is the bug in this code?
sousQuestions.reponse: maxSum is initialized to 0, so the function returns 0 for arrays with all negative numbers instead of the maximum (least negative) subarray sum.

sousQuestions.texte: How would you fix this bug? Write the corrected code.
sousQuestions.reponse: Initialize maxSum to -Infinity or arr[0]. Corrected: let maxSum = -Infinity; or let maxSum = arr[0]; with appropriate null checks.

Instructions: This is a full mock whiteboard coding interview. You will solve the problem, explain your thought process, discuss complexity, and test your solution.

Problem: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

Example 1: Input: s = 'abcabcbb' → Output: 3 ('abc')

Example 2: Input: s = 'bbbbb' → Output: 1 ('b')

questions.texte: Write your complete solution in JavaScript, explain your approach, discuss complexity, and test with examples.
questions.reponse: function lengthOfLongestSubstring(s) { let set = new Set(); let left = 0; let maxLength = 0; for (let right = 0; right < s.length; right++) { while (set.has(s[right])) { set.delete(s[left]); left++; } set.add(s[right]); maxLength = Math.max(maxLength, right - left + 1); } return maxLength; } Time: O(n), Space: O(min(n, alphabet)).
